name: Atomstack A5 Pro 5W
tagline: 5W Ultra-budget diode laser: minimum viable entry point
tldr: Atomstack A5 Pro 5W is the 5W SKU on the Atomstack atomstack a5 pro line. One of the cheapest ways to try laser engraving. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.

priceRange.note: 5W optical module: verify SKU before buying

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Cheapest way into the A5 Pro frame: $199–299, often less used
Large 410 × 400 mm bed for a 5W-class machine
Enough for engraving wood, leather and coated surfaces at hobby pace
cons: Atomstack's '40W' label on the A5 Pro is electrical input: its spec lists 5–5.5W optical output
Cutting tops out around 3 mm basswood; owners report 2 mm plywood at 250 mm/min in one pass and 3 mm needing 2–3 passes
Very slow fills: ~28–43 min for our 10 × 10 cm photo test
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 5W SKU on Atomstack A5 Pro. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Optimize for engraving: lower DPI on photos, higher scan speed on line art after test burns. Air assist still helps clarity. Compare benchmark times on the next tier before assuming you need more power.
primaryUse: Engraving-first desktop diode for makers who prioritize mark quality over cut speed
mainObjective: Detailed engraving on organics and coated metal: occasional thin cuts only

editorialDepth.advantages: Atomstack A5 Pro 5W suits makers who sell marks, photos, and gifts more than daily panel cutting. Reasonable open-frame entry price.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if you already quote 3 mm+ cutting in production: see 10W or 20W in the line. Not for cast acrylic or bare metal without spray.

faq.question: Is the Atomstack A5 Pro 5W really a 40W laser?
faq.answer: No. Atomstack marketed the A5 Pro as '40W', which is electrical input; its own spec gives 5–5.5W of optical output. Compare machines on optical power only: by that measure this is an entry-level engraver, not a cutter.

faq.question: What can the A5 Pro 5W cut?
faq.answer: Thin material only. A LightBurn forum owner reports 2 mm plywood at 250 mm/min and 100% power in one pass, and expects 3 mm to take 2–3 passes. Our profile caps basswood at 3 mm, and a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood takes ~14–24 min in our benchmark.

faq.question: The A5 Pro is discontinued: should I still buy one?
faq.answer: Only as a cheap used starter or remaining stock, ideally under $200. The A5 Pro is no longer a current Atomstack model, so check the module and power supply before paying. If you plan to cut 3 mm wood regularly, the 10W tier or a current 10W machine is a better first buy.

standoutFeatures.title: Lowest price of the line
standoutFeatures.body: $199–299 in our range and less on the used market, for a 410 × 400 mm engraving bed.

standoutFeatures.title: A low-risk learning machine
standoutFeatures.body: At 5W-class optical power, mistakes cost little: a sensible way to learn LightBurn, focus and material tests before buying bigger.
